title: Mica Therapeutics - Renewal & Region/Uplift Check-in
summary: Quick renewal check-in: customer considering 30% capacity uplift, add EU region and VPC/private pilot. Discussed SLA, KMS integration, timeline for contract amendment, and a short performance pilot for 2 weeks. Action items assigned for pricing sheet, security package, and pilot runbook.

transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2025-01-11
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Arianna (Redwood AE), Matt (Redwood SE), Jules (Redwood CSM), Priya (Mica VP Product), Carlos (Mica Head Infra), Erin (Mica CTO), Liam (Mica SRE)

Auto Summary (auto-generated, optional): customer wants a moderate uplift, EU presence, and an on-prem/VPC pilot to meet data residency. They want to see a short perf run and security package before signing extension.

--- Transcript body ---
[00:00] Arianna (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you squeezing this in. Quick intros?
[00:06] Priya (Mica): Hi, Priya here. I'm the VP Product at Mica. We've got Carlos and Erin on the infra/CTO side and Liam from SRE.
[00:13] Arianna: Perfect. Matt, Jules, quick intros?
[00:16] Matt (Redwood SE): Hi all, Matt here -- I'll be supporting the pilot and perf stuff.
[00:19] Jules (Redwood CSM): Jules, CS lead, will help coordinate timelines and contract questions.
[00:23] Priya: Great. The reason for the sync is twofold: one, we want to extend our current commitment for another year and two, look at adding EU region and a modest capacity uplift. Also need to confirm data residency and KMS integration options.
[00:35] Arianna: Understood. High level, what's the target uplift? Percent and burst behavior?
[00:40] Carlos: We're thinking roughly 30% steady-state uplift and a 2x burst window for campaign spikes. Right now, peak token throughput hits our 99th at about - uh - roughly 8k tokens per second across all apps.
[00:53] Matt: Okay, that maps. Do you currently route anything through a EU region today or is it all US?
[00:58] Erin: All US today. We have European customers and procurement is pushing data residency for EU customers. So we want a EU region instance with isolated data storage, and ideally KMS in our own tenant.
[01:10] Arianna: So two asks: EU region provisioning and KMS/HSM integration via customer-managed keys in your cloud. Both supported by Redwood Private and we can offer Dedicated in EU for isolation. Quick tradeoff: Dedicated/EU private option increases unit cost but gives quicker residency guarantee and separate tenancy.
[01:26] Priya: Right, procurement will prefer the Private/VPC path but cost is a factor. Can you give rough delta?
[01:32] Arianna: We'll put numbers in the quote, but ballpark: Dedicated in EU is about 25-35% premium versus hosted US. And there are options: a hybrid approach where control plane is hosted and inference runs in your EU VPC to limit cost.
[01:45] Carlos: And timeline? If we sign the amendment, how long to stand up EU region Dedicated?
[01:50] Jules: Usually 4-6 weeks for provisioning and validation, if we have KMS access patterns and network peering set up promptly. Pilot/bench can start earlier on hosted EU nodes though, subject to data residency constraints.
[02:03] Liam: Quick Q: For the pilot can we keep logs in our S3 and only tokenized telemetry in Redwood? We want to keep raw transcripts off platform.
[02:10] Matt: Yes, you can route logs to your S3; Redwood can flush user-level logs to customer buckets. We also have retention config and audit log exports. Note that some debug traces are only available on Dedicated/private paths.
[02:23] Priya: Good. On security, procurement asked for SOC2 and ISO docs plus network diagrams. Can you share that?
[02:30] Arianna: Absolutely, we'll share our security package. I'll attach SOC2, ISO 27001 summary, encryption-at-rest details, and our redwood-dedicated network diagram.
[02:39] Erin: When you say KMS integration, are we talking full HSM or just KMS envelope keys? We need HSM-level assurance.
[02:46] Matt: We support KMS envelope encryption with customer-managed keys in major cloud KMS. If you require HSM-backed keys, we can support cloud HSM providers via Bring-Your-Own-Key path; there are a few extra steps for signing and attestation. We'll include options in the security appendix.
[03:03] Priya: Excellent. For the perf pilot, we want a two-week window that hits realistic user patterns. Can Redwood run continuous streaming with KV cache warm-up? Our primary workload is streaming generative summarization (long context) so cache behavior matters.
[03:16] Matt: Yep. We'll provide a perf harness that simulates your 95/99 token distribution and continuous batching. Couple notes: for long contexts we recommend higher kv_cache memory and quantization profile X that preserves quality. There might be minor throughput tradeoffs but cost goes down per token if we use prefix caching.
[03:33] Carlos: When you say quantization profile X, sorry what is that?
[03:36] Matt: Oh, sorry, that's internal shorthand; it's the 8-bit qprofiling we test on our runtime. Sorry the transcription might show Q-profile or Q-profile X, it's basically an 8-bit mixed quant path that keeps logits fidelity high.
[03:46] Priya: Sounds like an SE deep-dive. We just need to know if quality regressions are possible.
[03:50] Matt: We'll include a quality baseline and automated evals tied to your prompt set so we can detect regressions during pilot.
[03:57] Arianna: Ok cash question: Do you want monthly billing or annual commit? We can show both. There is a lower unit cost on annual.
[04:03] Priya: Procurement leans annual but they want flexibility for a 3-month ramp. Possibly a 12-month with a 3-month addendum to increase capacity.
[04:12] Jules: We can do a 12-month term with scheduled ramp increments and an amendment window. I'll draft amendment language for staged increases and burst capacity.
[04:20] Liam: One small thing: network peering - do you support VPC peering or private link? We prefer private link to reduce exposure.
[04:27] Matt: We support PrivateLink and Interconnect in major clouds. For VPC peering we can do that too but PrivateLink gives finer control. We'll outline the network options.
[04:36] Priya: For procurement, can you itemize EU region add-on, Dedicated vs hosted, and KMS/HSM add-on separately? They want line items.
[04:44] Arianna: Yes. I'll include explicit line items and an annual vs monthly comparison.
[04:48] Carlos: Curious — any reliability SLOs for the Dedicated EU nodes? Do you offer a latency SLA or uptime SLA?
[04:54] Jules: Dedicated customers get an SLA — we'll include uptime targets and per-route latency SLOs; latency SLAs depend on the model family and sequence length but we can commit to availability. For latency guarantees we typically offer best-effort plus rollback/fallback policies into a lower-cost variant.
[05:10] Priya: Ok great. Any blockers from Redwood side to get pilot started next week?
[05:14] Matt: The main blocker is the perf script and a small sample dataset and the exact routing rules you want. If you share a sanitized sample and anonymized traffic trace, we can kick off hosted-EU pilot nodes in a couple days.
[05:26] Priya: We can get a sanitized trace by Friday.
[05:29] Arianna: Awesome. Let's recap next steps...
[05:32] Arianna: Redwood items: pricing worksheet with EU Dedicated and hybrid options, security docs and KMS/HSM notes, SE perf runbook and benchmark script. Mica items: procurement timeline, sanitized trace, and traffic percentiles. We'll target the pilot week of 2025-01-27.
[05:48] Priya: Sounds good. One quick question — you mentioned competitors feature parity for VPC peering, do you do region failover testing?
[05:57] Matt: Yes, we can simulate region failover and show failover latencies; we'll include a short failover test in the runbook.
[06:04] Erin: Also please include an example of audit log exports and retention caps. Procurement will ask.
[06:08] Jules: We'll include the export patterns and retention options in the security bundle.
[06:12] Arianna: Ok if no other Qs we'll wrap. Thanks everyone. We'll send the deck + quote + pilot runbook by next Thursday.
[06:20] Priya: Thanks all.
[06:22] Carlos: Thanks.
[06:24] Meeting ends.

Notes about transcription: occasional mis-hears ("qprofiling" vs "Q-profile"), speaker overlap around 03:30, partial words in SRE metrics. Some product names transcribed as "Redwood Dedicate" or "Redwood Privatee" in the auto summary.
questions: What is the EU region provisioning timeline?
Can logs be exported to customer S3 and raw transcripts excluded?
